title: 4.1–4.3 Catch-Up
contentObjective: I can show I am caught up on Lessons 4.1–4.3 by using each lesson's big idea in mixed practice.
languageObjective: I can explain which lesson's big idea I used and how, using key vocabulary from Lessons 4.1–4.3.

vocabulary.definition: A percent is a ratio that compares a number to 100, so every percent answers the question “how many out of 100?”
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje es una razón que compara un número con 100, así que todo porcentaje responde “¿cuántos de cada 100?”
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing a number to 100 is a ___.

examples.text: 65 shaded squares out of a 100-square grid is 65%
examples.why: It compares the part to a whole of exactly 100.
The whole is not 100, so the count is not the percent.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares a number to 100. The word means “per hundred,” and the symbol is %.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara un número con 100. La palabra significa “por cada cien” y su símbolo es %.
vocabulary.cloze: The word that means “per hundred” is ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.definition: The meaning hidden inside the word percent: for every group of 100. It is why every percent can be written as a fraction over 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El significado dentro de la palabra porcentaje: por cada grupo de 100. Por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como fracción sobre 100.
vocabulary.cloze: The meaning hidden inside the word percent is ___ ___.

examples.text: 3 out of every 10 rewritten as 30 out of 100
examples.why: It restates the ratio for a group of 100.

examples.text: 3 out of every 10 left as it is
examples.why: Until the whole is 100 you cannot read the percent off it.

vocabulary.definition: A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares. Shading squares shows a percent directly, one square per percent.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula de 10 por 10 con 100 cuadros. Sombrear cuadros muestra un porcentaje directamente, un cuadro por cada uno por ciento.
vocabulary.cloze: A 10-by-10 grid of 100 squares used to show a percent is a ___ ___.

examples.why: Each square is one percent, so the shading reads directly as 65%.

examples.text: A bar split into 8 unlabelled pieces
examples.why: Without 100 equal parts you cannot read a percent from it.

vocabulary.definition: A comparison of one part against the whole amount. In a percent, the whole is always 100%.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una comparación de una parte con el total. En un porcentaje, el total siempre es 100 %.
vocabulary.visual: The whole = 100%; the part = the percent
vocabulary.cloze: A comparison of one part against the whole amount is a ___ comparison.

examples.text: 18 students out of a class of 60
examples.why: The second number is the whole the part came from.
That compares two parts, not a part with its whole.

vocabulary.definition: More than one whole. A percent above 100 means the amount is larger than the thing it is being compared to.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Más de un entero. Un porcentaje mayor que 100 significa que la cantidad es mayor que aquello con lo que se compara.
vocabulary.visual: 150% of the gray kitten = 1.5 times its weight
vocabulary.cloze: A percent above 100 means the amount is ___ than one whole.

examples.why: One whole plus another half — more than the whole.
Half of one whole is less than the whole.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.
vocabulary.cloze: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole are ___, ___ and ___.

examples.why: All three name the same amount of the same whole.
0.2 is a different amount, so the set is not equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The percent divided by 100 gives the decimal.
Multiplying by a plain 35 makes the answer 100 times too big.

vocabulary.definition: A reasoned answer that is close enough to be useful, found without exact computation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una respuesta razonada, lo bastante cercana para ser útil, sin cálculo exacto.
vocabulary.example: 8.6% of 216 is about 10% of 220, which is 22.
vocabulary.cloze: A reasoned answer close enough to be useful is an ___.

examples.text: “About 20 pounds” when the exact answer is 18.576
examples.why: Close enough to plan with, found without exact computation.
That is the exact answer, not an estimate.

vocabulary.definition: A friendly percent — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — used as a landmark for estimating.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un porcentaje amigable — 1%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% — que sirve de punto de referencia.
vocabulary.example: 4 GB of 6 GB sits between the 50% and 75% marks.
vocabulary.visual: 1% · 10% · 25% · 50% · 75% · 100% — the landmarks you can find mentally.
vocabulary.cloze: A friendly percent used as a landmark, like 10% or 25%, is a ___ ___.

examples.text: Using 50% because half of an amount is easy
examples.why: It is one of the percents you can find in your head.

examples.text: Using 37% because it is in the problem
examples.why: It is exact, but nothing about it is mentally friendly.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 4.1–4.3: 4.1 Understand Percent, 4.2 Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages, 4.3 Estimate the Percent of a Number. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 4.1–4.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 4.1: A percent is a ratio comparing a number to 100. The whole is always 100%, so a percent above 100 means MORE than one whole. • 4.2: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent. • 4.3: Anchor the whole at 100%, mark benchmark percents, and place the amount between the landmarks it falls beside.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 4.1 — Understand Percent: A percent is a ratio comparing a number to 100. The whole is always 100%, so a percent above 100 means MORE than one whole.

Lesson 4.2 — Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages: To turn a fraction into a percent, build an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 100: ask “what do I multiply the denominator by to get 100?” and multiply the numerator by that same number. The new numerator is the percent.
Lesson 4.3 — Estimate the Percent of a Number: Anchor the whole at 100%, mark benchmark percents, and place the amount between the landmarks it falls beside.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 4.1: Shanice's gray kitten weighs 4 ounces. The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is the orange kitten's weight?
From 4.2: Let's change 1/5 into a fraction out of 100, then a decimal and a percent.
From 4.3: The Green-Team recycled 216 pounds of material; 8.6% was metal.

youDo.title: Show you're caught up
lines: The practice below mixes problems from Lessons 4.1–4.3. Each problem is tagged with its lesson number.
Stuck on one lesson's problems? Open that lesson from the curriculum menu for the full re-teach.

explore.label: Sort each estimation move: is it using a BENCHMARK PERCENT or COMPATIBLE NUMBERS?

cards.text: Treating 24% as 25% because quarters are easy
Changing 216 pounds to 200 pounds to divide easily
Using 10% of a number and scaling from there
Placing 4 GB between the 50% and 75% marks

explore.instructions: Sort all six, then tell a partner one estimate where you would use BOTH moves at once.

connect.scenario: Margaret's storage: 6 GB total, 4 GB used, and 3.5 GB of the used space is photos. The rest of the used space is mail, messages, and documents.
connect.promptQuestion: Of the USED storage, approximately what percent are photos — and why does the whole change from 6 GB to 4 GB for this question?
connect.prompt: The whole for this question is ___ . Photos are about ___ % of the used storage, since 3.5 GB sits between the ___ % benchmark and the ___ % benchmark on the number line.

check.stem: For the question 'of the USED storage, what percent are photos,' what is the whole (100%)?
choices: 10 GB, adding the total and used storage together
check.explanation: The whole is set by what the question is 'of' — 'of the used storage' makes the 4 GB used the new 100%, not the 6 GB total capacity.

check.stem: On a double number line built for a whole of 4 GB, what amount lines up with the 75% mark?
check.explanation: 75% of 4 GB is three-quarters of 4, which is 3 GB. 4.5 GB would be more than the whole itself, and 1 GB is only 25% of 4 GB.

check.stem: Photos take up 3.5 of the 4 GB of used storage. About what percent of the used storage is photos?
check.explanation: 3.5 GB sits between the 75% mark (3 GB) and the 100% mark (4 GB), much closer to 100% — about 87%. Reading 3.5 as 35% mistakenly treats 10 as the whole instead of 4.

connect.modelAnswer: For this question the whole is 4 GB, because we are asked about the used storage — the 6 GB total does not matter now. On a double number line for 4 GB, 75% is 3 GB and 100% is 4 GB. Photos take 3.5 GB, halfway between those marks, so photos are about 87% of the used storage.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) What does the word percent mean?
approaching.explanation: Percent means per hundred, which is why every percent can be written as a fraction with a denominator of 100.
choiceFeedback: Per ten would be a tenth, not a percent.
Per thousand is a different comparison entirely.
"Part" does not say how big the whole is; a percent always compares to 100.
hints: Look at the second half of the word: cent.
A century is 100 years; a cent is 1/100 of a dollar.
Percent = per 100.
approaching.explanationEs: Por ciento significa por cada cien, y por eso todo porcentaje se puede escribir como una fracción con denominador 100.
hintsEs: Mira la segunda parte de la palabra: ciento.
Un siglo son 100 años; un centavo es 1/100 de dólar.
Por ciento = por cada 100.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.1) 3 out of every 10 students walk to school. What percent is that?
approaching.explanation: Multiply both terms of the ratio by 10 to compare to 100: 3 out of 10 becomes 30 out of 100, or 30%.
choiceFeedback: 3 out of 100 would be 3%, but the ratio here is out of 10.
10 is the second term of the original ratio, not the percent.
That adds the two numbers instead of scaling the ratio.
hints: A percent compares to 100, so rewrite the ratio out of 100.
What do you multiply 10 by to get 100?
Multiply BOTH terms by that same number.
approaching.stemEs: 3 de cada 10 estudiantes caminan a la escuela. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplica los dos términos de la razón por 10 para compararla con 100: 3 de 10 se convierte en 30 de 100, o sea 30%.
hintsEs: Un porcentaje compara con 100, así que reescribe la razón sobre 100.
¿Por cuánto multiplicas 10 para obtener 100?
Multiplica AMBOS términos por ese mismo número.

choiceFeedback: Try again: 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 as well.
Build an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 — multiply the top and bottom by the same number.
hints: Percent means out of 100. What do you multiply the denominator 5 by to get 100?
5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the numerator by that same 20 to build the equivalent fraction.
3 × 20 = 60, so 3/5 = 60/100. A fraction out of 100 IS the percent.
hintsEs: Porcentaje significa de cada 100. ¿Por cuánto multiplicas el denominador 5 para llegar a 100?
5 × 20 = 100, así que multiplica el numerador por ese mismo 20 para formar la fracción equivalente.
3 × 20 = 60, entonces 3/5 = 60/100. Una fracción de cada 100 ES el porcentaje.

choiceFeedback: Double-check: 20 × 5 = 100, so the top must be multiplied by 5 too.
Scale 7/20 up to a denominator of 100 first.
hints: The denominator 20 is friendly: 20 × 5 = 100, and percents are always 'out of 100'.
Make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 by multiplying top AND bottom by the same number.
Multiply 7/20 by 5/5: the bottom becomes 100. Whatever the top becomes is your percent.
hintsEs: El denominador 20 es amigable: 20 × 5 = 100, y los porcentajes siempre son 'de cada 100'.
Forma una fracción equivalente con denominador 100 multiplicando arriba Y abajo por el mismo número.
Multiplica 7/20 por 5/5: la parte de abajo se vuelve 100. Lo que quede arriba es tu porcentaje.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.3) Margaret's phone has 6 GB of storage and 4 GB is used. About what percent is used?
approaching.explanation: 4 out of 6 is 2/3, which is about 67%, so 'about 70%' is the reasonable estimate.
choiceFeedback: That reads the 4 GB as 40% — but the whole is 6, not 10.
25% of 6 GB would be only 1.5 GB.
More than 100% would mean using more storage than the phone has.
hints: What is the whole?
4 out of 6 is the same as 2 out of 3.
Two-thirds is close to which benchmark?
approaching.stemEs: El teléfono de Margaret tiene 6 GB de almacenamiento y 4 GB están usados. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje está usado?
approaching.explanationEs: 4 de 6 es 2/3, que es aproximadamente 67%, así que 'aproximadamente 70%' es la estimación razonable.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero?
4 de 6 es lo mismo que 2 de 3.
¿Dos tercios está cerca de cuál punto de referencia?

approaching.stem: (Lesson 4.3) On the double number line for 6 GB, what amount lines up with 25%?
approaching.explanation: 25% of 6 GB is one quarter of 6, which is 1.5 GB.
choiceFeedback: 2.5 GB would be more than a third of the storage.
That divides 6 by 4.8 rather than by 4.
4 GB lines up near 67%, not 25%.
hints: 25% means one quarter.
One quarter of 6.
approaching.stemEs: En la recta numérica doble para 6 GB, ¿qué cantidad se alinea con 25%?
approaching.explanationEs: 25% de 6 GB es una cuarta parte de 6, que es 1.5 GB.
hintsEs: 25% significa una cuarta parte.
Una cuarta parte de 6.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.1) The orange kitten weighs 1.5 times as much as the gray kitten. What percent of the gray kitten's weight is that?
onLevel.explanation: The gray kitten is the whole, or 100%. One and a half wholes is 100% + 50% = 150%.
choiceFeedback: 15% would be a small fraction of the gray kitten, not more than all of it.
50% is only half the gray kitten's weight.
1.5% is a tiny sliver — but the orange kitten is heavier.
hints: Which kitten is the whole?
One whole is 100%. What is half a whole?
Add the whole and the half.
onLevel.stemEs: El gatito anaranjado pesa 1.5 veces lo que pesa el gatito gris. ¿Qué porcentaje del peso del gatito gris es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: El gatito gris es el entero, o 100%. Un entero y medio es 100% + 50% = 150%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál gatito es el entero?
Un entero es 100%. ¿Cuánto es medio entero?
Suma el entero y la mitad.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.1) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: A player scored 150% of the weekly goal of 200 points.
workedExample.workEs: Un jugador logró el 150 % de la meta semanal de 200 puntos.

workedExample.label: Step 3
workedExample.workEs: El jugador superó la meta de 200 puntos.

onLevel.correctWork: Step 2 reads the percent as if it were the points themselves. A percent is a comparison, not an amount: 150% of 200 points is 1.5 × 200 = 300 points.
onLevel.explanation: Step 3 even contradicts Step 2 — 150 points would fall short of a 200-point goal. A percent always needs a whole to be a percent OF.
hints: Steps 1 and 3 are both right — check Step 2.
150% of what?
onLevel.explanationEs: El Paso 3 hasta contradice al Paso 2 — 150 puntos no alcanzarían una meta de 200 puntos. Un porcentaje siempre necesita un entero DEL cual ser porcentaje.
hintsEs: Los Pasos 1 y 3 son correctos — revisa el Paso 2.
¿150% de qué?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.2) A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
onLevel.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
choiceFeedback: 8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
88% is the rounded version, but this score converts exactly. Divide 7 by 8 and keep every decimal place — the percent is not a whole number.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.
onLevel.stemEs: Un juego muestra tu puntaje como 7/8 completado. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
onLevel.explanationEs: 8 no escala a 100 con un número entero, así que divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, y 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. Eso es 87.5 de cada 100.
hintsEs: Prueba primero el paso de cada 100: ¿hay un número entero por el que puedas multiplicar 8 para llegar exactamente a 100?
No lo hay (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), así que usa el método de respaldo: divide el numerador entre el denominador.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, que es 87.5/100; desliza el punto dos lugares a la derecha para leer el porcentaje.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 4.2) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Divide the bottom by the top
workedExample.labelEs: Divide el de abajo entre el de arriba

onLevel.correctWork: The student divided in the wrong order. To turn a fraction into a decimal, divide the TOP by the bottom: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, then × 100 → 62.5%. So 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (A check: 5/8 is less than 1, so the percent must be under 100%, never 160%.)
hints: Is 5/8 more or less than one whole? Then can its percent be over 100%?
8 will not scale to 100 evenly, so divide the numerator by the denominator: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, which is 62.5/100 → 62.5%.
onLevel.explanation: The fraction bar means numerator ÷ denominator, so this division is upside down. It should be 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, and 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. A quick check catches it: 5/8 is less than one whole, so its percent must be under 100% — 160% was impossible.
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra de fracción significa numerador ÷ denominador, así que esta división está al revés. Debe ser 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, y 0.625 × 100 = 62.5%. Una comprobación rápida lo detecta: 5/8 es menor que un entero, así que su por ciento tiene que ser menor que 100%; 160% era imposible.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante dividió en el orden equivocado. Para convertir una fracción en decimal, divide el de ARRIBA entre el de abajo: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, luego × 100 → 62.5%. Así que 5/8 = 0.625 = 62.5%. (Una comprobación: 5/8 es menor que 1, así que el porcentaje debe estar por debajo de 100%, nunca 160%.)
hintsEs: ¿5/8 es más o menos que un entero? Entonces, ¿puede su porcentaje pasar de 100%?
8 no se escala a 100 de forma exacta, así que divide el numerador entre el denominador: 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625, que es 62.5/100 → 62.5%.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.3) The Green-Team recycled 216 pounds; 8.6% was metal. Using compatible numbers 10% and 200, the estimate is:
choiceFeedback: That is 1% of 200 — the decimal moved one place too far.
That subtracts 8 from 216 instead of taking a percent.
That reads 8.6% as 86 pounds.
hints: Write 10% as a decimal.
One tenth of 200.
onLevel.stemEs: El Equipo Verde recicló 216 libras; 8.6% era metal. Usando los números compatibles 10% y 200, la estimación es:
hintsEs: Escribe 10% como decimal.
Un décimo de 200.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 4.3) Photos use 3.5 GB of the 4 GB of used storage. About what percent of the USED storage is photos?
onLevel.explanation: The whole is 4 GB here. 75% of 4 is 3 GB and 100% is 4 GB; 3.5 sits midway — about 87%.
choiceFeedback: That uses 6 GB as the whole, but the question asks about the USED storage.
That reads 3.5 GB as 35% — the whole is 4, not 10.
3.5 out of 4 is clearly below 100%, but not that close to it.
hints: What is the whole for THIS question?
The whole is 4 GB, not 6.
3.5 of 4 is between the 75% and 100% marks.
onLevel.stemEs: Las fotos usan 3.5 GB de los 4 GB de almacenamiento usado. ¿Aproximadamente qué porcentaje del almacenamiento USADO son las fotos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Aquí el entero es 4 GB. 75% de 4 son 3 GB y 100% son 4 GB; 3.5 queda a la mitad — aproximadamente 87%.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el entero para ESTA pregunta?
El entero es 4 GB, no 6.
3.5 de 4 está entre las marcas de 75% y 100%.

extending.title: (Lesson 4.1) Find the error

workedExample.label: Setup
workedExample.work: Which is larger: 40% of 200, or 150% of 40?
workedExample.workEs: ¿Cuál es mayor: el 40 % de 200 o el 150 % de 40?

workedExample.label: Step 2
workedExample.work: So 150% of 40 must be the larger amount.
workedExample.workEs: Entonces el 150 % de 40 debe ser la cantidad mayor.

extending.correctWork: Step 2 compares the percents instead of the amounts. Each percent applies to a different whole: 40% of 200 = 80, while 150% of 40 = 60. Since 80 > 60, the first amount is larger — even though its percent is smaller.
extending.explanation: A percent is meaningless until you know what it is a percent OF. A small percent of a big whole can easily beat a large percent of a small whole.
hints: What is each percent a percent OF?
Compute both amounts before comparing.
extending.explanationEs: Un porcentaje no significa nada hasta que sepas de QUÉ es porcentaje. Un porcentaje pequeño de un entero grande puede superar fácilmente a un porcentaje grande de un entero pequeño.
hintsEs: ¿DE qué es porcentaje cada porcentaje?
Calcula las dos cantidades antes de comparar.

extending.title: (Lesson 4.2) Find the Conversion Error

workedExample.label: Divide numerator by denominator
workedExample.labelEs: Divide el numerador entre el denominador

hints: 2 ÷ 3 doesn't terminate — is 0.67 the exact decimal?
0.67 is rounded. The precise decimal is 0.666... (repeating), making the percent 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanation: The division is set up the right way, but 2 ÷ 3 does not end — it gives 0.666... repeating. Writing 0.67 rounds the value, so the percent it produces (67%) is rounded too. The exact answer is 66.7% or 66⅔%.
extending.explanationEs: La división está planteada correctamente, pero 2 ÷ 3 no termina: da 0.666... periódico. Escribir 0.67 redondea el valor, así que el por ciento que resulta (67%) también queda redondeado. La respuesta exacta es 66.7% o 66⅔%.
hintsEs: 2 ÷ 3 no termina — ¿0.67 es el decimal exacto?
0.67 está redondeado. El decimal exacto es 0.666... (periódico), lo que da un porcentaje de 66.7% o 66⅔%.

extending.stem: (Lesson 4.3) Two students estimate 8.6% of 216. Ana uses 10% of 220 = 22. Ben uses 10% of 200 = 20. Whose estimate is closer to the exact answer, 18.576?
choices: Ben's — 20 is 1.4 away; Ana's 22 is 3.4 away
extending.explanation: Exact is 18.576. Ben's 20 misses by about 1.4; Ana's 22 misses by about 3.4. Compatible numbers won this one.
choiceFeedback: 22 − 18.576 = 3.424, which is farther than Ben's 1.424.
The two distances are 1.4 and 3.4 — not equal.
Both are valid estimates; the question is which lands closer.
hints: Find each distance from 18.576.
1.4 versus 3.4.
extending.stemEs: Dos estudiantes estiman el 8.6% de 216. Ana usa 10% de 220 = 22. Ben usa 10% de 200 = 20. ¿Cuál estimación está más cerca de la respuesta exacta, 18.576?
extending.explanationEs: Lo exacto es 18.576. El 20 de Ben falla por unos 1.4; el 22 de Ana falla por unos 3.4. Los números compatibles ganaron esta vez.
hintsEs: Halla la distancia de cada uno a 18.576.
1.4 contra 3.4.
choicesEs: La de Ben — 20 está a 1.4 de distancia; el 22 de Ana está a 3.4
La de Ana — 22 está más cerca de 18.576

optional.explanation: A percent already compares to 100, so 9 out of 100 is exactly 9%.
choiceFeedback: 90 out of 100 would be 90%.
0.9% would be less than 1 out of 100.
That adds instead of reading the ratio.
hints: The ratio is already out of 100.
Percent means per hundred.
Read the first number.
optional.explanationEs: Un porcentaje ya compara con 100, así que 9 de 100 es exactamente 9%.
hintsEs: La razón ya está sobre 100.
Por ciento significa por cada cien.
Lee el primer número.

optional.stem: (Lesson 4.2) Your arcade scoreboard reads 0.25 of the level cleared. What percent and fraction match this score?
optional.explanation: Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = 25%. As a fraction, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
choiceFeedback: Remember: multiply the decimal by 100, or move the decimal point right 2 places.
Check your conversion — 0.25 as a percent should be higher.
Not quite. Move the decimal two places: 0.25 = ___%.
optional.stemEs: El marcador de tu arcade indica 0.25 del nivel completado. ¿Qué porcentaje y qué fracción corresponden a este puntaje?
optional.explanationEs: Mueve el punto decimal dos lugares: 0.25 = 25%. Como fracción, 0.25 = 25/100 = 1/4.
hints: A decimal, a percent, and a fraction can all name the same amount — percent simply means “out of 100”.
To turn a decimal into a percent, multiply by 100 (move the decimal point two places right). To turn it into a fraction, read the decimal using place-value words.
0.25 reads as twenty-five hundredths, so start the fraction as 25/100 — then move the decimal two places for the percent and simplify the fraction.
hintsEs: Un decimal, un porcentaje y una fracción pueden nombrar la misma cantidad: porcentaje significa simplemente «de cada 100».
Para convertir un decimal en porcentaje, multiplica por 100 (mueve el punto decimal dos lugares a la derecha). Para convertirlo en fracción, lee el decimal con palabras de valor posicional.
0.25 se lee veinticinco centésimos, así que empieza la fracción como 25/100; después mueve el punto dos lugares para el porcentaje y simplifica la fracción.

optional.stem: (Lesson 4.1) Sort each percent by how it compares to one whole.
optional.explanation: 100% is the dividing line: it means exactly one whole. Everything below is part of a whole; everything above is more than a whole.
hints: What percent equals one whole?
Compare each number to 100.
99% is just under; 101% is just over.
optional.stemEs: Clasifica cada porcentaje según cómo se compara con un entero.

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 4.3) Estimate 19% of 71 using benchmarks — no exact computing.

steps.promptEs: Redondea 19% a un porcentaje de referencia: ___%.

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Benchmarks are the percents you can do in your head — 10% slides the decimal, 50% halves, 20% is double 10%.
Start like this: Round 19% to a benchmark percent: 20%.
parallelPractice.explanation: Round 19% to a benchmark percent: 20%. Round 71 to a friendly number: 70. 20% of 70 = 14.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Estima el 19% de 71 usando puntos de referencia, sin calcular exacto.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Los puntos de referencia son porcentajes mentales: 10% corre el decimal, 50% es la mitad, 20% es el doble de 10%.
Empieza así: Redondea 19% a un porcentaje de referencia: 20%.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: Redondea 19% a un porcentaje de referencia: 20%. Redondea 71 a un número amigable: 70. El 20% de 70 = 14.
